app.title: Polyglot Assist
app.no_answer_hint: Is the integration loaded? Settings → Devices & services → Polyglot Assist.

tips.how: Polyglot listens first to every voice command. If it knows the sentence, it carries it out right away, without AI and in the language you spoke. Otherwise it passes it on to your AI assistant.
tips.proposals: This is where Polyglot collects new, changed and to-be-removed commands, sentences and names. None of it is active until you accept it. Every suggestion has been checked: it must not interfere with any other command, and everything that already works must keep working.
tips.starter: The AI looks at your scripts, scenes and devices that Polyglot doesn't understand yet and suggests commands and names in all selected languages, plus types for your commands. Ideal for the first setup.
tips.newdev: After adding a new integration or device: Polyglot finds what's new and suggests names and commands.
tips.coverage: How many example sentences there are per language. Orange: one language has noticeably fewer variants than the others. With “Translate” the AI suggests the missing ones.
tips.safety: Normal: the command runs right away. Security-related (e.g. front door, garage, car): it runs, but is marked; Polyglot never accepts suggestions for it automatically, and you get a warning when changing it. Off: Polyglot ignores the command and the sentence goes to your AI assistant.
tips.groups: Type: lights, energy, weather … (can be set for each command). Polyglot works out the room and device from the devices a command controls.
tips.cats: Types organize your commands. You can add your own, rename them or delete them. When you delete a type, its commands move to “Other”.
tips.syntax: [square brackets] = optional · (a|b) = one of them · {placeholder} = a room, device or number that Polyglot fills in.
tips.answer: Speak: “Couch light on.” Sound: a short chime (needs Polyglot TTS). Only applies to control commands; questions are always answered out loud.
tips.kind: Control command: does something (light on …). Question: gives you information (weather, status …) and is always answered out loud.
tips.test: Type a sentence the way you would say it. Polyglot shows whether and how it understands it. Nothing gets switched.
tips.corpus: Real sentences from your everyday life that must always be understood the same way. Polyglot checks them before every change; if something would break, nothing is saved.
tips.names: What you call rooms and devices in each language, e.g. living room = Wohnzimmer = salon. These names don't change anything in Home Assistant itself and don't slow down your AI assistant.
tips.monitor: Polyglot remembers the last 500 voice commands (text only, no audio, stays in your Home Assistant). Once a day your own AI looks at what often wasn't understood directly and turns it into suggestions.
tips.languages: The languages spoken in your home. Polyglot detects them automatically; languages you deselect are no longer considered.
tips.aitask: The AI task that suggests translations, names and commands. It must not have any tools: it reads sentences from elsewhere and must not be able to control anything while doing so.
tips.builtin: Home Assistant comes with ready-made voice commands: lights on/off, dimming, color, timers, date, time, status. On its own, though, it only understands them in the language of your voice assistant. With this switch, Polyglot recognizes them in all selected languages and carries them out right away, without going through the AI. That's faster and also works when the AI can't be reached. Polyglot never controls doors, locks, gates, alarms or the car this way; such commands still go to your AI assistant. Only turn this off if you want to define all commands yourself.
tips.followup: So that your AI assistant understands “and now the piano too”, it is told what Polyglot just switched.
tips.fallback: Your AI assistant, which answers everything that isn't a fixed command.
